How to play

Keyboard and mouse

  • A / D move, W or Space jump or swim up, S drop or dive
  • Click and hold to use the held item: mine, attack or place
  • 1–9 or wheel pick a hotbar slot
  • E bag, H hide or show items, R army, F talk, trade, tame, cook or open chests, L aim lock, K quick save, G fly or walk in creative (and as the Dragonborn), hold B to breathe fire as the Dragonborn. You can change these in Settings.
  • Q cycle orders, M map, F trade or free a captive, Esc menu

Touch

  • Arrow pads move, jump, swim and dive
  • Tap and hold the world to use the held item, or switch to joysticks in Settings
  • Tap a villager or the Trade button to shop

New in Beta 0.9.68

Cover and bracing are for battles between the three factions: you, your soldiers and the enemy factions' soldiers. The guards of the wizard towers and the sky and magma castles don't take cover behind walls or brace in a line.

Beta 0.9.67

Sturdier shared worlds: when the host switches to another app or tab, their world keeps running for everyone, so friends are no longer left waiting or dropped. A friend's game no longer runs enemy village guards, scouting parties, sky knights or enemy village growth on its own (the host runs them for everyone), and the numbers that tell enemies and animals apart carry on when the host starts the world again, so a friend's tamed animals never get mixed up with new ones.

Beta 0.9.66

A deeper underground: new worlds go twice as deep below the islands, and the sea floor still reaches all the way down to the magma realm. The lowest caves, just above the magma realm, are winding tunnels with pockets of lava instead of one huge open cavern. Cave floors have rounded edges like the hills, and underground pools of water and lava are rounded bowls with ragged rims and air pockets instead of boxes. Older worlds get the tunnels, the lava pockets, the rounded edges and the rounded pools wherever nobody has explored yet. Saved worlds now go to the browser's larger storage, so bigger worlds and more of them fit.

Beta 0.9.65

Smoother shared worlds: a friend in your world sees enemies and animals glide smoothly instead of jumping, even on a slow connection. Their hits show at once (the number, the sound and the push) and the host applies them with the weapon's own knockback, kills vanish as soon as the host confirms them, every enemy hit reaches them, and their game knows which enemies are after them.

Workplaces level up: the woodcutter's lodge, the farmhouse and the miners' hut go from level 1 to 3 like every shop (Buildings, Village). The head worker asks a favor first. Each level makes room for 2 more workers and they bring in more, level 2 adds a loft with a bed and level 3 lanterns, a chimney and a banner. Five new cave monsters: cave bats in every cave (swarms in the dripstone caves), armored jade crabs, glowing rose wisps that throw bolts, azure spiders whose bite slows you, and fossil raptors that pounce in packs. More monsters lurk underground.

Formations: give your party the Formation order (in the Army window, or press Q until it says Formation). Your soldiers line up in ranks facing the nearest enemy, three to a block: the toughest melee soldiers in front, the next rank right behind them striking over their shoulders with longer reach, and archers and wizards behind you. The line holds its ground instead of chasing, and the front rank braces, taking less damage and knockback from the front. Any soldier, yours or an enemy's, standing shoulder to shoulder with two others braces the same way, so a packed enemy line is harder to break. Cover: a block or a door beside you, on the side a shot comes from, turns some shots aside (about a third with a low wall, more than half with full cover), and archers and wizards prefer targets standing in the open.

Beta 0.9.64

Favors before upgrades: before a shopkeeper upgrades their shop, they ask you for something from their own trade. The blacksmith wants ore or diamonds, the cook wants meat, eggs or honey, the fisher wants fish, the shipwright wants logs or pearls, and so on. What they ask for changes from world to world. Bring it, tap Give in their shop, and the upgrade opens. Growing your village works the same way: the quartermaster asks for supplies first (Buildings, Village). The Jeweler moves in once your village is a Town and the Archmage is beaten, and the War engineer once it is a City and you have taken an enemy castle. Rooms are lit by torches and lamps: a closed room with no torch is dim even at midday, and only windows and openings let daylight in. Every room your village built gets a torch once.

Beta 0.9.63

Trap doors: doors that lie in the floor, made at a workbench from any wood's planks, castle stone, deep stone brick or iron bars. Closed, you stand on one and nothing comes up through it. Tap it to open or shut it, jump up under it, or hold down while standing on it; it opens for you and shuts as soon as you are through. Your soldiers and tamed animals can follow you through, but enemies never open one. In your castle, the ledges up from the great hall end in trap doors that match the castle's stone, deep stone or iron, and the upper floor's west doorway has a door where a bed used to stand, so the upper floor is sealed off as your safe room.

Beta 0.9.62

Gem weapons: at a workbench, the Iron, Gold and Diamond weapon of a kind (Silver, Gold and Diamond for staffs) plus 4 gems make a special one, and the gem decides what it does. Bows and staffs: ruby burns (Fire bow, Ember staff), sapphire splits arrows or chains lightning (Tri-shot bow, Tempest staff), emerald blasts or wards (Blast bow, Ward staff), amethyst pierces every enemy in its path (Void bow, Void staff). Knights, macebearers and Beastmasters get thrown weapons, a glaive, flail or kunai for each gem: ruby burns, sapphire chills, emerald heals you a little each hit, amethyst flies farther and knocks back harder. No weapon you can have before the diamond tier beats a Diamond weapon. Grow meal (from bones, or seeds, glowcaps and berries at a composter, and left by your farmers each morning) grows a crop a stage or a sapling into a tree. Beat both wizards to unlock the Breakdown bench: next to it, any crafted item in your bag breaks back into all its materials. Your castle's arrow slits turn dark slate and then iron as it grows, nothing spawns on top of your buildings, and the chimney on a level 2 shop house sits on its roof.

Beta 0.9.61

Rugs lie flat on the floor, covering the top of the block they sit on, and come in six kinds: wool, blue, green, golden, striped and a bamboo mat. Jade, rose quartz and azure crystals hang from ceilings and grow out of cave walls like amethyst, and mining the block that holds a crystal knocks it loose. Enemies take fall damage. Accessories and charms turn up in chests half as often. Bows and staffs say their material: Wooden bow, Iron bow, Wooden staff, Gold staff. Settings, Screen layout has sliders for the checklist, the menu icons and the action buttons, and the choice list that opens with F has the X too.

Beta 0.9.60

Lava lies only underground, in puddles, pools and lakes of many sizes, each a bowl with air above it; lava that sat on the surface in older worlds has cooled to stone. Friends who join a shared world can tame the host's animals (they become the friend's own pets and the host's wild one goes away) and feed them for breeding, and a friend's game no longer makes stray enemies or animals of its own that the host never sees.

Beta 0.9.59

The wood of medium and tall trees stays behind the leaves: their wide trunks no longer show through the crown. The ground under houses, lodges, the castle and every building you place stays flat, with no slanted blocks below them. Lava sets you on fire (a cooling band or better ward stops it), and animals that wander into lava burn and die. A new world starts without the buildings of the world you played before.

Beta 0.9.58

Rain never builds up: it leaves no puddles and brings no floods at any weather strength, and the weather choices on the New world screen say so. Any old rainwater still lying in an older world dries up the next morning.

Beta 0.9.57

Bombs throw up much more smoke, and smoke hangs in the air longer (about 45 seconds); rain, storms and snow clear it from the open air two to five times faster. A ballista, cannon or trebuchet can only be set up when a free soldier in your party is with you, and that soldier works it. Press F beside a crewed machine (or use the Army window) and choose Aim, then click or tap a spot: the crew fires at enemies near the mark, or at the mark itself. "Own targets" lets it choose again. War machines are drawn at close to their real size next to you. In the test world a soldier joins you to work a machine if none is free.

Beta 0.9.56

Sugar bakes into sugar cake, berry tart, sugar cookies and candied apples at a furnace. Sea treasures make things: eight ancient coins and a gold bar make a Lucky coin charm, an old compass becomes a Dragon compass or an Astrolabe, two golden fish with pearls make the Lucky lure (or roast one into a golden fish feast), a sunken crown with pearls becomes the Tidecrown charm (+20 health, +20 mana, faster mana), Kraken ink with a black pearl makes the Shadow cloak, and coral presses into pink coral blocks. The Sage charm's faster mana refill works.

Beta 0.9.55

Mana refills faster the more mana you have: a wizard gets back 12% of their maximum mana every second and everyone else 8% (never slower than before), so mana crystals and other mana upgrades also speed up the refill. Wizards start with 90 health. The Archmage tower has about half as many guards. Items that shared a name have their own now: the Kraken's treasure-chest daggers are Tidebond daggers, the chain-lightning staff is the Tempest staff, and the mushroom you eat is a Glowcap. Metal bars, gems, crystals, mana potions, farm goods and sea treasures all have descriptions.

Beta 0.9.54

The red faction's light roof tiles are a brighter red instead of pink.

Beta 0.9.53

When a boss falls in a shared world, every player gets their own copy of its loot; coins and everything else on the ground go to whoever picks them up first. Blasts, cannon shots and fires leave smoke that drifts up and fades over about 20 seconds and piles up in a big battle: it greys the view, and arrows and spells shot through it spread from 5% in a light haze up to 35% in thick smoke. Rain and storms still fall but leave no water on the ground and bring no floods, and fog days come in light, normal and thick. Days and nights last twice as long (10 minutes of day, 4 of night). The castle's whole second floor is the safe room. While you are away, your world keeps going (up to 3 days): crops grow, and woodcutters, farmers and miners bring in their work. Stone buildings have light roofs in your faction's colour. Underground there are jade, rose and azure caves with glowing crystals, stalagmite caves, root caverns with glow bulbs and fossil beds.

Beta 0.9.52

A grappling hook that has bitten holds a taut, straight line from your hand to the claw while it pulls you in and while you hang; the rope no longer folds over into a loop above you.

Beta 0.9.51

Paths run along the ground between the buildings of your village and grow with it: trampled dirt for a Hamlet, cobblestone for a Town and an iron walkway for a City. Enemy villages have them too. You can also make all three to lay your own: dirt path from dirt, cobblestone path from stone, iron walkway from iron and stone.

Beta 0.9.50

Houses no longer show a strip of sky behind the floor between their second and third storeys: every building fills small gaps in its back wall. The castle's halls keep the same light wherever you stand, lit by their torches and lanterns; an open door no longer floods a building with daylight.

Beta 0.9.49

Every villager needs a home with a bed, a chest and the item of their trade: an anvil for the blacksmith, a cooking pot for the cook, a herb rack, a barrel for the fisher, a gem bench, a ship's wheel, a drafting table, a powder keg, a weapon rack for the Quartermaster, a notice board, a feed trough, a composter for farmers, a chopping block for woodcutters and an ore cart for miners. Your village's buildings come furnished; if one of the three goes missing, that villager stops working until it is back. Build your own home anywhere near the village (a closed room with walls, floor, roof, back wall and a door, plus the three items) and a villager of that trade moves in; the Buildings window lists every home and lets you move villagers. A Guard post placed in any such home becomes a soldier post. Furniture comes in stone, deep stone and iron and changes with the building. Roofs are your faction's colour at the stone and iron stages, and enemy villages grow through the same stages in their own colours. Every building lays dirt under itself and levels the ground to its neighbours the same way.

Beta 0.9.48

Your castle starts as stone, turns to dark deep stone for a Town and iron for a City. Stone doors and iron doors can be crafted at the workbench, and village buildings use them at their stone and iron stages. Woodcutters, farmers and miners now start with a wanderer: give one the job and they become its head and build the lodge, farmhouse or mine; then the Quartermaster hires up to 5 of each for 50 coins. The miners' hut grows from wood to stone to iron with your village, and the mine shaft has a platform across its top. The top shop house keeps its red tile roof without the turrets, its back walls have no gaps, and its balcony lantern hangs under a little canopy. The lodge and farmhouse stand level with your village, and the ground between neighbouring buildings is flat, with a slope only past the last one. The small tower has nothing over its hatch, so you can jump up to the roof. In the test world every building and upgrade is free.

Beta 0.9.47

Crafting is a grid of pictures: things you can make right now light up and come first, and tapping one shows what it needs, what you have, where it is made and Craft, ×5 and Max buttons. Star a recipe with Pin to keep it at the top. More tabs split the long lists: Furniture, Lights and decor, Materials, Farm and animals, Boats and machines, Potions and runes. The chest window shows your bag on the left and the chest on the right, sized to fit the screen, with Take all first. A shop house at level 3 gets a red clay tile roof with a turret on each corner instead of gold trim.

Beta 0.9.46

The portal on top of the stone keep stands in the middle of the roof (keeps you already built move it there). The wiki shows every building in your village at each step: the castle as a Hamlet, a Town and a City, the village houses, a shop house at levels 1, 2 and 3, and the woodcutter's lodge and farmhouse, with what each upgrade costs.

Beta 0.9.45

Watchtowers, keeps and small towers have arrow slits on their roofs, so the soldiers posted up top shoot through them too; the watchtower has 6 posts (two on each upper floor and two on the roof). Each building in the Buildings window has its own picture, and the animal pen shows a fence with crops and a sheep. The wiki has a Buildings section: every building with its cost, size and a picture of each numbered soldier post.

Beta 0.9.44

Archers and mages posted in towers, keeps and on roofs see over the wall beside them, aim at enemies far below and reach a little farther, so they shoot at whatever comes at their side of the building. Raiders always arrive from outside your village: any enemy soldier found on a village roof is put back on open ground outside, and monsters never appear on your roofs. The battlement wall is a small tower: one room with a doorway on each side, arrow slits over the doors and a lookout roof (4 posts). The orc huts are built of solid log walls, not tree trunks you could walk through. Every wood has its own plank wall and its own furniture look: spruce grain, birch flecks, palm weave, jungle vines and dark oak gold studs, and furniture has a dark outline so it stands out against any wall. Barrels, cupboards and desks store items, and you can sit on chairs, benches and stools to heal three times as fast. The miners' chest opens like any other chest.

Beta 0.9.43

Watchtowers have no glass: the bottom room is solid wall over the doors, and every floor above has arrow slits where the guards stand, so they can shoot out. The top room of every tower, yours and every faction's, is 4 blocks tall. Keeps have slits upstairs and solid walls over their doors. Window walls are a back wall of glass panes (4 from 1 glass and 1 stick at a workbench): the sky shows through and daylight comes in. Every table, chair, bench, stool, bed, bookshelf, cupboard, desk, barrel and workbench comes in all six woods; oak pieces take any planks, the others take their own wood. Planks of every wood sell for the same, and so do logs. New saplings: a pine sapling (a spruce sapling and 2 snow) and blue, green, red and orange mushroom spores (from the caps of giant mushrooms) that grow giant mushrooms on stone, moss, dirt or grass. The Herbalist sells every sapling and spore.

Beta 0.9.42

Every building in your village follows the same wood, stone and iron steps as the castle: the huts, battlement walls, watchtowers, animal pens and keeps you build yourself, and the outposts and keeps you capture, are wood in a Hamlet, stone in a Town and iron in a City, together with the castle, the houses, the lodge and the farmhouse. Shop houses keep following their own shop level.

Beta 0.9.41

Your buildings show how far your village has come. As a Hamlet your castle, houses, woodcutter's lodge and farmhouse are wood: plank walls, timber beams and thatch roofs. Growing into a Town rebuilds them in stone with tiled roofs, and a City rebuilds them in riveted iron with iron roofs. Each shop's house follows its own shop level instead: wood at level 1, stone at level 2, iron at level 3. Wood can catch fire in raids and storms, stone cannot, and iron plate takes an iron pickaxe to break. Furniture, doors, windows and chests stay where they are. Thatch, iron plate, iron beams and iron roofs can be crafted at a workbench too.

Beta 0.9.40

Melee leaders lift the fighters around them. Every beastmaster, knight and macebearer, you or a soldier, helps everyone on their side within 8 blocks, themselves included: beastmasters make them 10% faster, knights make them take 15% less damage and macebearers make them hit 15% harder. One of each kind counts, and enemies get the same from their own leaders. The lifts you have show under your coins. Faction bonuses reach every soldier of that color: archers and wizards shoot faster and their arrows and bolts fly faster, and macebearers reach farther.

Beta 0.9.39

In a shared world every friend has a health bar over their head, under their name: a gold-framed bar with a heart that turns from green to yellow to red, and flashes when they are close to falling. Soldiers keep their thin red line, so friends are easy to tell apart.

Beta 0.9.38

Checklists: every building, growing the village and each shop upgrade has a Checklist button. It pins a small list to your screen showing how many of each item you have and need, with a check mark once you have enough. When everything is there the list glows "Ready!", and it goes away once you build or upgrade. You can pin up to 3, and choose where they sit and how big they are in Settings > Screen. The health, mana and hunger bars are bigger, with icons, notches every tenth, a pale trail that drains after a hit, and a flash when one runs low.

Beta 0.9.37

Bird cages work for everyone in a shared world: a friend can put a bird in any cage, every player sees the birds and the eggs they lay, and eggs one player collects are gone for the others.

Beta 0.9.36

New worlds: the wizard tower stands alone on a small island of its own. Caves are richer: big caverns have rock pillars with ore in them, ledges with hanging stone and boulders; winding tunnels run from narrow crawlways to wide galleries; and small buildings with chests hide beside the caves: miners' camps, stone shrines, deep vaults and crystal grottos with gold chests, and mushroom huts. Worlds you already have keep their caves and tower exactly as they are.

Beta 0.9.35

Grappling hooks fire straight where you aim the moment you press X (or let go of the Hook dial), bite the first wall, ceiling or ledge in their path and pull you there; each hook reaches farther (10, 16, 24 blocks) and has its own colors. New permanent accessories: a Tackle box, Angler's earring and Lucky lure for fishing; a Cooling band, Ward amulet and Dragon scale ward against burning, frost, knockback and lava; a Sprinter's anklet and Shadow cloak to dash by double-tapping left or right; the Swift and Windrunner boots are back; and a Wayfinder stone opens the travel map anywhere with free trips. Some are sold by the Jeweler and Fisher, some are crafted, and the best drop from bosses. Beating the Goblin Beastmaster opens a portal at his war camp, and beating Grukk one in the middle of the orc island.

Beta 0.9.34

Animals: boars give boar meat and beavers beaver meat, and hawks, eagles, owls and penguins each have their own meat, raw and cooked. Pigs live in the grasslands (pork when hunted). Birds of every kind go in a bird cage (crafted at a workbench), never a fenced pen, and lay eggs there each morning; use the cage to collect them or let a bird out. As pets, only birds gather; other animals produce or collect food in a pen: cows milk, sheep wool, pigs mushrooms and carrots, boars grass and seeds, rabbits berries and carrots. Piglets, beaver kits and fluffy chicks of hawks, eagles and owls join the other babies. Runes say exactly what they do at each level.

Beta 0.9.33

Woodcutters and farmers work like the miners. The first woodcutter builds a woodcutter's lodge beside the village, and the first farmer a farmhouse with a field. Each has a chest and a head worker: talk to the Head forester or Head farmer to open it. Woodcutters fell trees, plant saplings where they cut and when trees run short, and bring the logs to the lodge. Farmers harvest and replant ripe crops, till and sow the farmhouse field, and bring the harvest in. They work wherever you are, have their own look, and friends see them too. Boats are an upgrade like an accessory: your best boat is always with you, and you sail it as soon as you walk into water. Penned and gathering animals bring produce instead of meat (cows give milk); plant eaters never bring meat, while hawks, eagles and bears can, and gatherers bring things a quarter less often. Axes and hoes have new icons.

Beta 0.9.32

Shared worlds live online: whenever a world is hosted on the game page, it is saved online every few minutes. If you join with the game ID while nobody is hosting, you open the newest copy and host it yourself; when the first host comes back, they get the newest copy too. Your hero stays your own. Every friend sees the enemies and shots around them, wherever they are, and the group shares one monster limit. Anyone can grow the village into a town or city, and it grows for everyone. Wear as many different charms as you like: their bonuses add up, and the bag's Charms worn row takes one off. Bread is made from wheat only.

Beta 0.9.31

Shared worlds: jump or swim onto a friend's boat to ride along (jump off toward land to leave), and everyone sees the soldiers sitting in a boat, the armor each player wears, and fires burning anywhere near them. Soldiers come along through realm portals. Break the frozen winter sea with a pickaxe or axe (the hole freezes over next morning). Chests have a Sort button: by type, name, value or amount. Trophies are a 2 by 2 picture of the boss and hang straight on a back wall; no shelves needed. Miners, woodcutters and farmers keep working however far away you are (woodcutters bring their logs home again, and climb over steps that blocked them). Boats say how many soldiers they carry in the shop and in crafting. The goblin forest sends a few ambushes a day instead of an endless stream, and water far from every player waits instead of flowing, so friends' games run smoother.

Beta 0.9.30

Trading with friends: stand within 5 blocks of a friend and press T (on a phone, the use button, then Trade with). A trade window opens for both of you: tap items in your bag to put them on the table, add coins, and both press Accept to swap. Changing an offer takes back both Accepts, and F no longer hands items over. Raids on your village are gentler: none before day 5, then a small chance each morning of 1 to 3 soldiers, growing by 1 or 2 every 5 days. Raiders land on open ground outside your village, never on a roof or inside your walls. Blocks go down over animals (they step aside), and tapping an old block while holding a different block swaps them, with the old one going into your bag. Chests have a Stack button that joins stacks of the same item. In shared worlds, enemies are just as active around every friend as around the host, and castle guards wake for whoever walks in. Hiring a woodcutter or farmer no longer freezes the game.

Beta 0.9.29

Split stacks: select a stack in the bag (or in a chest on a phone) and a Move slider appears with 1, Half and All; tapping another slot, dragging or Drop then moves only that many. On a computer, right-click a stack to pick up half, or right-click in a chest to send half across. Charcoal: burn a log of any wood in a furnace. Torches take a stick and a charcoal (coal works too) for four. In shared worlds everyone sees trees fall, a friend's logs pop out at the stump for everyone to see, friends who join see the host's explored map, and a player who leaves disappears with a "left the game" message.

Beta 0.9.28

Worlds can have names. Type one on the New world screen (or leave it blank), rename a world any time from Continue with the Rename button, and see the name in the save list, the pause menu and the multiplayer Recent list.

Beta 0.9.27

Grass slowly grows back over bare dirt that touches grass and is open to the air, so dug-up or placed dirt greens over in a few minutes and the grass keeps spreading. Tilled soil, and dirt under a block or under water, stay as they are. On a computer the top bar shows every button again (Bag, Craft, Army, Buildings, Full screen, the eye, Menu and Minimize); phones keep the shorter bar with the ⋯ More button.

Beta 0.9.26

The wiki has a phone layout: a bar along the bottom (Back, Home, Search, Contents, Play), a big search box with large results, a slide-out menu, recipes and tables shown as cards that fit the screen, long lists that show the first few with a Show all button, and long pages folded into sections you tap open.

Beta 0.9.25

The wiki is its own app at pumped60.github.io/dragon-amulet-wiki, with its own icon, and it works offline. Add it to your Home Screen beside the game. The Wiki link on the title screen opens it without closing the game: on Android it opens the wiki app, and on iPhone a Safari window with a Done button that takes you back.

Beta 0.9.24

Woodcutters, farmers and miners start with a wanderer: the first one you give each job becomes its head and builds the lodge, farmhouse or mine. Then hire up to 5 of each from the Quartermaster for 50 coins. Upgrading a shop changes its house: level 2 lifts the roof for a third floor with the shopkeeper's bedroom, lanterns and furniture for the trade (weapon racks and armor stands for the Blacksmith, tables and stools for the Cook, desks for the Jeweler, barrels for the Fisher and so on). Level 3 adds a balcony with a railing, a red tile roof with a turret on each corner, a banner on the roof, paintings, rugs and a showpiece for the trade.

Beta 0.9.23

Growing your village (into a town, then a city) and the report on the opposing villages (their food, gold and army, Watch a commander, gifts to villages you conquered) are in the Buildings window, under your buildings and defense posts. The Army window keeps your party, soldiers, animals, war machines, expeditions and hiring.

Beta 0.9.22

Phones: tapping a button (Bag, Army, Buildings, More and the rest) no longer pops up its name. On a computer the name still shows when you hover the mouse over it.

Beta 0.9.21

Silver armor sits between wooden and iron armor (4.5 defense, 15 silver bars), like the silver tools and weapons. If you wear iron armor, you keep it. In shared worlds, everyone sees each other's lit bombs flying and on the ground, the pieces a blast throws, and the rubble from anyone's bomb, which crumbles away after three days.

Beta 0.9.20

Phones: swiping sideways or down on a menu or the death screen can no longer take the browser back or reload the page and drop you out of the game.

Beta 0.9.19

Phones: buttons and taps on the world stay lined up after you turn the phone sideways, and small buttons are easier to hit. In the bag and in chests, hold an item for a moment to pick it up and drag it to another slot, or tap it (you see its name) and then tap the slot where it should go. In a chest, tap an item twice to send it straight across.

Beta 0.9.18

On phones, the ✕ in the top corner closes every menu and pop-up, including the pause menu, the ⋯ More menu and the eye's list, and never taps the button underneath. Tapping an item shows just its name; tap the name to see its picture and every stat. Settings has tabs (Controls, Screen, Sound, World, Computer). Under Screen you can choose what tapping an item shows (name only, short, everything or nothing) and stand the item bar and the health, mana, XP and hunger bars up and down instead of across.

Beta 0.9.17

Two treasures to find in chests. The Dragon compass shows which way the dragon's lair lies and how far; without it you can't tell. The Astrolabe shows the season, the weather and the days until the next season; without it the clock shows only the day. One compass always waits in the goblin warcamp's gold chest, the Jeweler sells astrolabes, and the test world starts with both.

Beta 0.9.16

Trees are back to their original look: the trunk reaches a round crown and the leaves sit over it.

Beta 0.9.15

The eye (under ⋯ More, or H) opens a "Show on screen" list with everything ticked: untick the item bar, health bars, info lines, mini-map or a button and it hides at once; tick it to bring it back. Hide everything hides it all in one go. In shared worlds every player sees bomb blasts and the bosses' warning marks (the Sky Ranger's wind ring and target, the Magma Knight's glowing cracks).

Beta 0.9.14

A calmer top bar: Bag, Army, Buildings, the God menu (test world), Menu and ⋯ More. Crafting is a tab at the top of the bag (C still opens it). Speed sits with the other switches in the God menu. On phones the Fly button sits beside Torch. Full screen, Hide items, Quick save and Hide the buttons are under ⋯ More.

Beta 0.9.13

Tidier item screens, especially on phones and in the test world. The God menu shows items, soldiers, enemies and animals as a grid of tiles (tap one to take or spawn it), with quick filters for weapons, tools, armor, blocks, food and materials. Creative "All items" uses the same tiles. On phones, crafting shows two recipes side by side in shorter cards, and its tabs scroll in one row. The day, coins and party lines in the corner sit on a soft dark backing, so they stay readable.

Beta 0.9.12

Settings > Torches lets you choose how torches work: what a tap does with the Torch button on (place a torch, or light only), whether double-tap places a torch, whether tools rest while the torch is on, and whether holding Shift lights your torch on a computer.

Beta 0.9.11

Phones: in Stick and tap, the pickaxe always mines the nearest block toward where you tap, so it never jumps between blocks. The Torch button lights your way and turns taps into torch placing: one tap puts a torch exactly where you tap, and your pickaxe, axe, hoe and hammer rest until you switch it off (weapons still swing). Double-tap still places a torch when the Torch button is off.

Beta 0.9.10

The Dragon Amulet wiki: a page for every item, recipe, class, monster, boss, animal, shop and crafting station, all linked together, with search. Open it from the title screen or at pumped60.github.io/dragon-amulet-wiki. The Multiplayer menu lists your recent shared worlds with their codes: tap Host again or Join to go straight back in. Arrows and spells shot by soldiers, enemies and bosses fly the right way on every player's screen.

Beta 0.9.9

Silver gear: a silver sword, mace, daggers, bow, staff, pickaxe, axe, hoe, hammer and fishing rod sit between wood and iron. Smelt silver ore (found just below the surface, above iron) into silver bars at a furnace and craft them at a workbench, or buy them from the Blacksmith. Each is halfway between the wooden one and the iron one; the silver rod catches the same fish as the wooden rod with less junk and quicker bites. Shops sell crafted things for half of what their materials are worth, and there is more iron in the ground. Pickaxes clear grass and plants, a double jump breaks a fall, weather can be switched off (new world or Settings), the phone move stick sits on the left (Settings moves it right for left-handed players), friends see your grappling hook, and the Dragonborn's fire (hold B on a computer) stops at the ground.

Beta 0.9.8

In a shared world everything matches for every player: a tree someone cuts falls for everyone, back walls and new village houses show up whole, a wanderer given a job by any player becomes the same shopkeeper, miner or soldier for all, and friends' arrows fly the way they were aimed. Water falls through platforms, slides down slopes and stairs, and is drawn in front of furniture standing in it. Rain and floods leave half as much water, and penned animals stay in until the water is three quarters of a block over the fence. On the surface a roof alone no longer makes it dark: only a space closed in on every side with a back wall is dark. Storms and rain last 12 hours of game time, and the water they leave drains away within the next 6. Mouse aim lock starts switched on (L or Settings turns it off). The Mac and Windows apps fetch the newest game each time they start.

Beta 0.9.7

Every menu (bag, crafting, shops, chests, army, map, settings, help and the rest) has an X in the top right corner that stays put however far you scroll. On phones you always sprint while moving (switch it off in Settings), double-tap anywhere in the world to place a torch, and the Torch button switches your hand-held light. Joysticks are the starting touch controls again; "Stick and tap" puts a move stick on the right and lets you tap anywhere to mine, build or attack there. Every class button in the new world screen is the same size, with the Dragonborne weapon tally just under them.

Beta 0.9.6

Play on a Mac or Windows computer in its own window: open pumped60.github.io/dragon-amulet-play in Chrome or Edge and press "Install on this computer" on the title screen (or the install icon in the address bar). It gets its own icon, works offline and updates itself. There are also downloadable Mac and Windows apps on the Releases page of the dragon-amulet-play project on GitHub. F11 switches full screen in the downloaded app.

Beta 0.9.5

Fire: anything that can burn (wood, planks, furniture, leaves, plants, grass) catches fire and burns with flickering flames, spreading a little to what it touches before burning out to charred wood, ash or nothing. The Dragonborn's breath, fire bombs, lava, lightning, fire arrows and raiders all start it; water and rain put it out, and it never spreads into your own village. Standing in it burns.

Every kind of tree has its own sapling (oak, spruce, birch, palm, jungle and dark oak): a felled tree drops saplings of its own kind, the Herbalist sells the ones you have found, and each grows into its own tree. On phones, tapping an item shows its name and a few words about it, and new gear says what it does in a short line; choose Full in Settings for every detail. The test world skips the opening screen, and a Dragonborn there starts with all five dragonborne weapons.

Beta 0.9.4

Phones: two-finger controls, like Terraria. The first finger you put on the game screen moves you wherever it lands: drag left or right to walk, up to jump or fly up, down to drop or dive. A second finger aims at the spot it touches and uses what you hold (attack, mine, build) for as long as it stays down; a quick tap still talks to villagers and opens chests. The Hook and Fire dials stay at the bottom right. You can switch back to joysticks or buttons in Settings.

The Dragonborn's red wings beat like the white sky wings when he is in the air, his tail sways as he moves, and on phones his fire breath has its own Fire dial next to the Hook dial: touch it to breathe, drag to aim the fire, let go to stop.

Beta 0.9.3

The Dragonborn can always be tried out in the test world. For new survival and creative games he stays greyed out until you defeat Vorthax in a survival world; wins in the test world or in creative never unlock him or the dragonborne weapons (Vorthax still drops the weapon there).

Beta 0.9.2

The Dragonborn, a sixth class: half dragon, he flies whenever he likes and breathes fire (hold B, or the Fire dial on phones), burning enemies and scorching wood and grass, using mana. He has the most health, armor and mana of any class. He shows in the class list from the start, greyed out until you defeat Vorthax in survival; after that he is unlocked on this device for every new character.

Dragonborne weapons: defeating Vorthax drops the dragonborne weapon of your class (sword, bow, mace, staff or daggers), and every hit from it sets enemies burning. Each one you win is unlocked for good, and a new Dragonborn starts with all of them. Beat Vorthax with every class to collect all five; the tally under the Dragonborn shows which you have.

Beta 0.9.1

Bombs: craft black powder (2 coal and a bone), small bombs and fire bombs at a workbench, and buy big and sticky bombs from the Demolitionist. A small bomb is thrown and bounces before it blows; a fire bomb bursts where it lands and sets everything around it burning; a sticky bomb sticks to the first wall or enemy it touches; a big bomb is set down at your feet, so get clear. Every bomb breaks blocks: they burst apart in pieces, some of which land as rubble that crumbles away after three days, and the blocks around the blast are left burnt. Your own bombs hurt you and your soldiers at half strength, and they never break anything in your own village.

The Demolitionist moves into your village, with a house of his own, once the Goblin Beastmaster is beaten. Every shopkeeper's shop has three levels: talk to them to upgrade it with coins and building materials, and each level sells better goods. Level 2 needs a Town and level 3 a City. Upgraded houses get lanterns, then a red tile roof with turrets and a banner, and the shopkeeper shows gold pips over their head.

Beta 0.9.0

Bosses form one ladder, each harder than the last and each needing soldiers beside you: the Goblin Beastmaster (3), the Archmage (4), the Magma Wizard (5), the Sky Ranger (6), the Magma Knight (8), Grukk (10), the Kraken (12) and Vorthax (20). The wizards fly, teleport and chase you out of their towers; the Beastmaster vanishes and strikes from behind; the Sky Ranger hurls everyone back with a gale and marks a target for a fast arrow; the Magma Knight's armor glows and turns most blows aside until four fighters hit it, and fire erupts from glowing cracks in the floor. Enemy villages gang up on anyone who comes alone, so bring at least 5 soldiers.

The best weapons are thrown: Adamantite swords, the Magma blade and the Adamantite and Kraken daggers fly out and come back like a boomerang, and the Adamantite mace swings on a chain (hold to whirl it, let go to throw). Runes have levels I to V. Boss trophies are 2 by 2 replicas of the boss, standing on trophy shelves hung on a back wall.

The world has rolling hills and slopes, mist clouds, flowing lava you can swim in (and build over), flash floods, pumpkins, birds of prey and baby animals. The sky tower and the magma maze hide their rooms in fog. Craft grappling hooks to swing up to ledges, and buckets to carry water or harden lava. On phones the game fills the whole screen, the Hook joystick throws your grappling hook, and every window fits a short screen. Faces have matching eyes in every color.

Beta 0.8.0

Storm ore: when lightning strikes open ground in a storm it leaves a scorched hole with 3 to 5 blocks of storm ore around it. Smelt 3 ore into a storm bar at a furnace and craft storm tools, weapons and armor, a tier between diamond and mythril. Storm bars also make a lightning rod, which draws strikes to itself and leaves ore around its foot, and a storm charm. Storm ore and bars sell well.

Taking an enemy base: once its warlord is dead and three quarters of its people are gone, the faction surrenders and you choose to take its last soldiers into your army or execute them. Either way the castle is yours. Enemy castles have a second floor like yours. Your castle has a locked safe room upstairs where villagers hide from raiders; when the raiders are gone they come back down. Rain water dries up by the next morning.

The sky castle and the magma keep's throne rooms are reached from the top floor, with ledges down inside, and guards stand with each boss. The knights in the small guard towers by the wizard towers hold the ground floor. The dragon stays above your roofs during a raid and only attacks people outside. The Kraken's sunken chest opens once the Kraken is slain. Chests are always two blocks wide and furnaces two by two, and nothing behind them shows through any more.

Beta 0.7.2

Furnaces and orc blast furnaces are drawn as one solid block, two wide and two tall, with no gap at the top. Castle flags sit on top of their tower roofs instead of hovering above them.

Beta 0.7.1

Hold Shift and click to place a torch wherever you point, whatever you are holding (as long as you have torches). Axes, hoes and hammers have new pictures with the head across the top of the handle. On a phone, tap the Torch button, then tap where the torch should go. Craft shears (2 iron bars at a workbench) or buy them from the Beast trainer (40 coins), and use them beside a sheep for 2 to 3 wool; its wool grows back in a day.

Beta 0.7.0

Your castle is twice as tall. The portal is on the new second floor, with a throne and beds, and when raiders reach your village your villagers run upstairs to hide. Villagers can now be hurt; a new one moves in a day after one falls. Hire woodcutters and farmers from the Quartermaster, and every boss you slay (+10%) or enemy warlord you kill (+5%) makes all your villagers bring in more each day, up to double. Expeditions walk home to the Recruiter, who hands you their loot.

Kill a faction's warlord inside their base when only a tenth of their soldiers are left and they surrender: the survivors join your army. Raiders burn wooden buildings, and siege engines blast walls on both sides. Enemy factions keep the coins from monsters they kill alone, unless you hit the monster too. Factions clear the goblin forest and the orc island before moving into their towers. Their workers dig stepped quarries, light tunnels with torches and climb out of holes.

The sky castle and the magma keep are different from each other, each room stays dark until you step in, and each throne room has a real throne. The four castle bosses have new moves: the Sky Ranger dashes and shoots from mid-air, the Magma Knight charges through fire and leaps, the Archmage floats and makes mirror images, the Magma Wizard calls meteors and fire from the ground. Grukk drops a war maul and the Kraken fang daggers, and every boss drops a token to call it back for a rematch in its own lair. Wizard towers have a guard tower on each side, knights below and wizards above. The dragon's embers fill his whole cave, his gold is one heap you scoop up as you walk into it, and every 5th day he may fly out for a minute to raid a village, maybe yours.

Charms: wear one at a time for a small bonus (faster attacks, longer shots, more damage, health, speed and more). They drop from strong enemies, turn up in treasure chests, and the plainer ones are sold by the jeweler. The shipwright sells boat upgrades. Fishing casts a real line, with sharks, sea finds and rare seasonal fish on the best rod. Weather is set when you make a world (light, medium or strong): lightning burns trees, rain fills hollows and drains away, snow settles in winter and melts in spring, and rain patters on your roof. Trees tip over when cut and their leaves fall; plants break with the block under them. Drag an item onto another in the bag or a chest to swap them. Hold Shift to light your way without a torch in hand, and Shift + right-click places a torch.

Beta 0.6.1

Enemy villages live like colonies. Their woodcutters fell trees and plant saplings, quarrymen dig, farmers harvest and replant, and everyone carries their load home. Builders put up houses, farms, walls, castle expansions and watchtowers one block at a time, so you can watch a village grow, or stop it. Each new house brings more villagers, workers and soldiers. The Quartermaster in your castle can grow your own village. On phones, tapping the hotbar shows an item's name, and tapping an item in your bag shows its full stats for a few seconds.

Beta 0.6.0

Enemy armies sail. They march to the shore, launch a ship, cross the sea and land, island by island, so you can meet them at sea. Sink an enemy ship for its coins and gold. Sail near an enemy island and they send a patrol ship after you. Deck cannons (siege workshop, or tier I from the shipwright) let your longships and warships fire back. Enemy workers carry their goods home, so stopping them hurts their faction.

Grow your village from a hamlet into a town and a city in the Buildings window, for more houses, room for more soldiers, a jeweler, and later the war engineer and warships. Conquered villages grow loyal and send tribute, or rebel if you neglect them. Set runes into your weapons (fire, frost, life, mana or keen), and add more of the same rune to level it up from I to V. Your soldiers rank up as they fight and learn shield wall, volley or pack hunter. Your bestiary makes you stronger against monsters you hunt. Send soldiers on expeditions for loot. Seasons change every 6 days: in winter the sea freezes and anyone can walk across it, and storms make sailing slow. Bosses drop trophies, 2 by 2 replicas of the boss, to mount in your village for small permanent bonuses. A trophy stands on two trophy shelves side by side, and the shelves hang on a back wall.

Doors come in every wood. Archers hit harder with bows and their arrows fly through a second enemy. The test world lets you pick your class. In multiplayer, enemies fight your friends' soldiers and pets, and friends can save the shared world as Friend's world and keep playing it if the host leaves.

Beta 0.5.1

The sky realm's cloud islands sit closer together, with small cloud stepping stones between them. Mythril ore now looks like a pale teal cloud block, and its veins are three times bigger. The magma realm is twice as wide, with much more adamantite. The Sky Ranger and the Magma Knight drop the top permanent upgrades you don't have yet: Swiftness III first, then Sprint III, then hearts of vigor and of the arcane. The test world always gives you a recall mirror.

Beta 0.5.0

Your bag holds the hotbar plus 6 rows of 9, and chests hold 9 rows of 9. Drop an item by dragging it out of the bag window or onto Drop. The Gear locker in your bag keeps your tools and weapons without using bag space. Craft All makes as many as you can; hold a Buy, Sell or Craft button to repeat it. Every villager buys the goods of their trade. Chests can sit underwater. Furnaces, workbenches and chests show their full size before you place them. Torches can replace grass and flowers (not trees), and give no light underwater.

The taming whistle is now a permanent upgrade (80 coins). With it, any class tames animals for 1 food (small animals), 2 (medium) or 3 (big ones). Beastmasters tame without food. A row of 4 or more fences on the ground makes a pen: walk tamed animals in and choose to let them stay, or give an animal the Farm job and it settles in by itself. Penned animals produce goods each morning. Fences are drawn in front of you.

Mythril ore forms inside the sky realm's clouds once the Sky Ranger falls, and adamantite in the magma realm once both realm bosses fall; chests no longer hold those bars. Bosses enrage at half health. Enemy fighters flank you, their archers pick off the weakest target, and wounded commanders call their soldiers. Enemy factions build only on open ground, away from buildings. Capture an enemy outpost or keep by clearing its guards. Conquering a castle frees its prisoner. Your shopkeepers offer tasks. Slaying the dragon leads to an ending and new game plus.

Multiplayer: friends who join get the host's real world, see your portals and boats, can trade within 5 blocks (T opens a trade window), share chest contents, and can jump to each other by tapping a friend on the map or the arrow pointing at them. They come back where they left off.

Islands and the sea

Each faction lives on its own island across a wide sea full of sharks, jellyfish, piranhas and eels. Swim if you dare, bridge across with blocks, or build a boat. A raft carries only you and sits low enough for sharks to bite. A canoe is fast and safe. Rowboats, longships and warships carry 2, 5 and 9 soldiers. Hold a boat to pick it, otherwise your biggest one is used. Soldiers who don't fit wait on shore.

Starting out

You begin alone in the wild. Find the abandoned village on your island. It has a crumbling castle and houses that are rebuilt in perfect condition when you claim it. It becomes your home, where you respawn, hire soldiers and change class. The 3 to 5 drifters (3 to 5) living there join you, and you choose whether each becomes a shopkeeper or a soldier. More soldiers come from freeing prisoners in enemy castles, bandit camps and caves, or hiring them at home. A recall mirror teleports you home.

Building shapes

Craft stairs, slopes and half blocks from planks, stone brick, castle stone, marble, dark planks or sandstone. Or use a shaping hammer on any placed block to cycle it through half block, slopes, stairs and back.

Plants and fishing

Saplings grow into trees, berry bushes ripen (tap to pick), and bamboo and cacti grow taller. Herbalists sell seeds and brew with herbs. With a fishing rod, tap near water to cast. When the bobber dips and a "!" appears, tap again quickly to reel in your catch. Visit the fishing village for rods.

Fishing

Better rods catch more: wooden (common fish), iron (bass, cod, pufferfish, pearls), gold (tuna, anglerfish, jewel boxes) and mythril (swordfish, golden fish, crowns, black pearls). Ocean, lakes and cave water hold different fish. Junk sells for a coin or nothing; throw it away with Delete in your bag. Open jewel boxes, sealed chests and bottles by using them.

This update

Your bag holds the hotbar plus 6 rows of 9; anything extra stays on the ground. Drag items between slots with the mouse or a finger; hover an item to see its picture and stats. Press F with several things nearby to pick one from a list. Tools and weapons are crafted with sticks (from planks), and any wood works in wooden recipes. The first tier of every tool is now wood (copper is gone). Adamantite ore is only found in the magma realm, mythril only in the sky realm's clouds, and only after their bosses fall. Cows give beef, sheep give mutton and wool (wool makes beds). Enemy faction islands have watchtowers full of archers and mages at both ends, and the goblins keep a wooden lookout on their forest shore. You can give up to 5 villagers of a conquered village new jobs. A second great ocean on the far side of the world hides the Kraken and its sunken treasure.

Portals, realms and factions

Your faction is the abandoned castle you claim; the other two colors are your enemies. Claiming your village, conquering a castle or freeing a camp prisoner opens a portal (on castle roofs). Click a portal to open the map, then tap another portal to travel with your army to your home, freed camps, allied or conquered castles, the wizard tower, the magma fortress, and (once their wizards are dead) the sky and magma realms. Each trip costs a few coins. Each realm has a huge castle with 20 to 30 soldiers and its boss in a throne room at the far end. The Sky Ranger (5,000 health) and the Magma Knight (6,000 health, twice the reach, burning blade) need an army to beat. You start in wooden armor; every armor set changes your look, with a crest in your faction's color. Cannon, blast-bow and other explosions break blocks (75% drop), and fire arrows scorch grass, trees and wooden buildings. In the test world, the Speed button in the God menu runs the world at 2x, 5x or 10x.

Thrown weapons

The Adamantite sword and the Magma blade are thrown: attack to send the sword spinning out, and it comes back to your hand like a boomerang, cutting everything it passes both ways. The Adamantite mace swings on a chain: tap to hurl it, or hold to whirl it above your head and let go to hurl it wherever you are aiming at that moment. The Adamantite daggers and the Kraken daggers are thrown one after another, up to 3 at a time, and each comes back like the sword.

Bosses, in order

Beat the bosses in this order, each harder than the last: the Goblin Beastmaster (bring 3 soldiers), the Archmage (4), the Magma Wizard (5), the Sky Ranger (6), the Magma Knight (8), Grukk the Ogre King (10), the Kraken (12) and Vorthax (20). With fewer soldiers or fighting pets near a boss than it needs, only a little of your damage gets through and it heals; the boss bar shows how many you have with you. The Beastmaster vanishes into the shadows and strikes from behind. The two wizards fly, teleport around you and chase you out of their towers, landing now and then (that is your chance with a sword). The Sky Ranger's gale hurls everyone back, and a red mark on someone means a fast arrow is coming: move. The Magma Knight's armor glows white-hot and turns most blows aside until four different fighters hit it, and glowing cracks in the floor mean fire is about to erupt there.

Armies

Bring soldiers. Enemy villages and outposts gang up on anyone who comes alone: with fewer than 5 of your soldiers or pets beside you, the whole garrison turns out, hits you much harder and shrugs off most of your blows. Vorthax needs your whole army: the more of your 20 soldiers fight beside you in the lair, the harder your blows land and the less it heals, and the more often it lands where swords can reach it. The boss bar shows how many of your fighters are with you.

New this update

Test world (title screen) starts a normal world in save slot 4, with a God menu for giving any item, upgrading gear, recruiting soldiers and spawning enemies or animals, plus a world speed button. It starts with a prepped farm nearby, and the God menu's World tab builds more farms, ripens crops, skips to morning and sets the weather (rain, thunderstorm, snowstorm, flash flood, lightning, any strength). Ice islands are all snow, with small ice huts guarded by frost archers (slowing arrows) and frost brutes (shatter into ice); neither burns in the sun. Big caverns have rock islands and pillars. Penguins and polar bears gather fish. Growth dust from the herbalist makes a plant grow a stage and 50% faster afterwards. A war engineer arrives once the Sky Ranger and Magma Knight are both defeated. Mini-bosses now use set attack patterns.

Farming and trees

Trees come in oak, birch, spruce, palm, jungle and dark oak, each with its own wood, planks, stairs and leaf color. Leaves only fall with a tree if they are connected to it through other leaves. With a hoe, left-click tills soil and right-click clears plants and harvests (on a phone, use the Hoe: Till / Break button). Crops grow in 3 stages: breaking stage 1 gives nothing, stage 2 gives a seed, stage 3 gives the crop and 1 to 2 seeds. Swords cut tall grass, which can drop wheat seeds. Sugar cane grows beside water, up to 4 tall.

Tools and the blacksmith

Every tool can be crafted at a workbench. Your blacksmith (or one in a conquered village) can upgrade the tool or weapon you are holding to the next tier for bars and coins. You can knock down trees with your bare hands, slowly. Pickaxes break blocks at half their old speed. Use the search box on the crafting screen to find a recipe. Save from the Menu.

Wings, lava and the deep

Sky wings let you fly up, steer and dive for 10 seconds. Once you have them, sky feathers from the sky realm raise that to 15, 20, 25 and 30 seconds, and the fifth feather gives endless flight. Lava now flows, slows you down and burns, unless you wear the top armor. The bottom of the world is unbreakable black bedrock. Diamond is a new tier between gold and mythril for every tool, weapon and armor.

Permanent upgrades

Swiftness and sprint elixirs, life and mana crystals, and other permanent boosts are only found in the sky realm and the magma realm. The herbalist sells hearts of vigor and hearts of the arcane (+20 max health or mana), but each one costs much more than the last. The strongest sprint elixir makes sprinting 75% faster than normal sprinting.

Armies, bows and staffs

Enemy castles hold about 15 soldiers led by a Warlord, who orders charges, retreats and raids. As a Beastmaster, each tamed companion (up to 3) boosts every ally's attack by 5%. Arrows fly straighter; the adamantite bow fires homing arrows, and the fire, blast and tri-shot bows fire burning, exploding and triple arrows. The adamantite staff fires homing bolts, the storm staff chains lightning, the ward staff shields you and your allies, and the ember staff burns.

Tools and farming

Pickaxes break blocks and mushrooms. Axes chop trees, bamboo, cacti and mushroom trees. Hoes till grass or dirt into soil and clear plants; plant wheat, carrot or pumpkin seeds on tilled soil and harvest ripe crops with the hoe. Saplings and berry bushes grow faster on tilled soil. Hammers break back walls and reshape blocks. Every tool upgrades from copper to adamantite.

Computer shortcuts

Hold Shift while moving to sprint 20% faster. You can attack while sprinting. While you hold Shift with torches in your bag, light glows around you, and clicking places a torch instead of using what you hold. Alt + click also places a torch. Use Full screen (under ⋯ More on the top bar) for a bigger view. Food and potions have a 5 second cooldown.

Beds and wings

Craft a bed (10 planks, 2 herbs) and sleep in it at night to skip to morning; it becomes your respawn point. Sky chests hold sky wings: hold jump in the air to fly for up to 15 seconds. They recharge on the ground. Sky chests stay sealed until the Sky Ranger is defeated; walk up to any sealed chest to see what it needs. Water washes away plants, crops and torches. From the map you can travel straight to the fishing village or any of your fishermen.

Your people

Soldiers keep up with you, heal when out of combat, and fallen soldiers never return, but a reserve soldier from your garrison steps in and comes to you. Fishers can be a villager job. On the map, choose whether each shopkeeper works at home or in a village you have conquered. Talk to the mine foreman to pick what each miner digs.

War machines

Build a siege workshop, then craft a ballista (long range), cannon (explosive) or trebuchet (huge boulders from far away). Use the item to deploy it; it rolls along behind your army. Assign a party soldier as crew in the Army panel and it fires on its own, including at the dragon, or press F beside it to climb on and fire it yourself. Longships carry 1 machine, warships carry 20 soldiers and 3 machines.

Burned villages at night

Fog rolls in and ghosts appear. One hit destroys a ghost. Every 2 to 5 nights a ghoul (four times as tough as a knight) rises in one ruin and always drops a rare weapon for your class.

The magma realm

Deep below the world lies a red cavern realm, sealed from above. Defeat the magma wizard in his fortress to open a portal down. The Magma Knight rules the realm from his keep. You can dig your way up to leave.

Zooming

Hold Ctrl and scroll, or pinch with two fingers, to zoom the game view.

Your army and the dragon

The dragon can be beaten with a full party of soldiers fighting beside you. The Quartermaster in your castle sells permanent upgrades to your soldiers' armor, weapons and training. A wanderer made a miner becomes your mine foreman and builds a hut over a mine shaft; then hire up to 5 miners from the Quartermaster, who dig and carry ore back up to the hut's chest.

The sky realm

A shimmering barrier in the sky stops you from flying or building up to the clouds. The only way up is the portal at the top of the wizard's tower, guarded by mages and the Archmage. When he falls, a portal opens where his body lay. The realm covers a quarter of the world's width, with scattered cloud buildings and the Sky Ranger's moated castle at its far end. Its drawbridge lowers as you approach. In the sky you'll find cloud islands, temples with sky chests, and tough sky knights. Jump down to return (watch out for fall damage), or use the portal.

Taming and cooking

Beastmasters tame animals without food. Other classes need the taming whistle and 1 to 3 food. In the Army panel, set each animal as a pet (it can't be hurt), a fighter (it fights, but if it dies it's gone), a gatherer (it collects resources near you, and beavers chop trees), or a farm animal (it stays in a fenced pen). Near a furnace, open the Cooking recipe book to cook meat. Cooked food heals far more.

Wildlife

A colored dot above an animal shows its temper. Green animals never attack. Yellow ones fight back if you hit them. Red ones will hunt you. Animals drop meat.

Army

Open the army panel to give orders (follow, defend me, hold here, charge) and to place soldiers into your 8 party slots. Hire soldiers or change your own class at home. Free captives at bandit camps on wild islands to recruit them.

Upgrades and building

Crafting or buying a better tool or weapon upgrades the one you have instead of adding another. Armor and accessories like swift boots, the cloud charm (double jump), the diving helmet, lanterns and mana rings are worn automatically and stay with you. Build chests to store things, and decorate with marble, red brick, dark planks, tiles, stained glass, lanterns, fences, bookshelves, doors and background walls.

The dragon mountain

The dragon lives at the edge of the world, at the top of a tall mountain. Climb to the cave mouth near the summit.

Mining and magic

Caves run deep. Better ores need better pickaxes: iron needs copper, gold and emerald need iron, ruby and mythril need gold, adamantite needs mythril. Life and mana crystals found in caves raise your maximum health and mana. Staffs use mana, and wizards cast the strongest spells.

Trading

Villagers of your own faction trade with you from the start. Another faction's villagers only trade once every one of that faction's soldiers is defeated. Sell ore, bars and gems for coins.

Joysticks: the left stick moves (push up to jump, down to drop or dive). Drag the right stick toward where you want to mine, build or attack and hold it. You don't need to tap each block.

Villagers

These drifters were waiting in the abandoned village and want to join you. Make each one a shopkeeper, a woodcutter, farmer or miner (the first of each becomes the head of a lodge, farmhouse or mine), or a soldier for your army. You can come back and talk to them later.

Game references

Dragon Amulet is an original game, made with love for the games that inspired it:

  • Minecraft (Mojang Studios): mining, crafting and building a world block by block.
  • Terraria (Re-Logic): side-view exploration, deep caves, a hotbar, bosses, and a move-and-aim touch layout.
  • King Arthur's Gold (Transhuman Design): medieval knights and archers, and a chunky pixel-art look.

All names belong to their owners. No art, code or assets from these games are used.

Multiplayer

Play together in one world. Everyone who opens this game's link can join with the room code. Everyone plays on the host's side, and the host's world is the one that is saved.

Recent worlds

Host a game

Set up a new world as usual; you get a room code to share.

Or reopen a world you hosted before; your friends rejoin with the same code and keep their progress.

Join a game

Choose a character

Characters keep their gear, upgrades, soldiers, pets and coins, and can play in any of your worlds or in someone else's multiplayer world.

Skills

Each level gives one skill point. Learning a skill gives you its ability even if you have never found the item. Items you find (boots, charms, helmets, rings, lanterns) also need the same level before they work. Sky wings need level 15 and the dragon amulet level 20.

Dragon Amulet

You wake up alone on an island the ember dragon once burned.

Find the abandoned buildings and claim the old castle as your home. Build an army, conquer the rival factions, and slay the dragon to claim the Dragon Amulet.

Buildings

Choose a building, then tap or click the ground where it should stand (within 40 blocks). Materials come from your bag; any wood works for planks and logs.
